newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASEAN institute urges Cambodian ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN institute urges Cambodian ceasefire.

text.p: The ASEAN Institute of Strategic and International Affairs (ISIS) on Thursday appealed to the two prime ministers of Cambodia to stop fighting and begin talks to settle their differences.

The Singapore-based institute said in an open letter to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen that the fighting in Cambodia was likely to affect regional stability and security.
"We therefore most earnestly urge Your Royal Highness and Your Excellency to cease all armed hostilities and commence peaceful dialogue to resolve differences amicably," it said.
"The development is particularly unfortunate since it has occurred on the eve of the planned admission of Cambodia into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN)," it added.
The publication of the letter coincided with an emergency meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers in Kuala Lumpur to discuss Cambodia and its application for membership.
Cambodia was due to become a member of ASEAN, along with Burma and Laos, at the grouping's annual meeting at the end of this month in the Malaysian capital.
But Hun Sen's ousting of Ranariddh over the weekend has cast doubt over that plan.
At least 58 people have died and up to 200 have been wounded in clashes between forces loyal to the two leaders.
The ASEAN ISIS letter said it noted with dismay the unravelling of the political order that had been painstakingly established in Cambodia following United Nations-sponsored elections in May 1993.
It made no other comment on Cambodia's bid for membership of ASEAN.
Current members of ASEAN are Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
